SMTO-EXE-0022 — The Python code for this step has a mistake

GUID: d9970861-2327-4931-8a62-980bed2e4d4d
Slug: python-source-invalid
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • The Python code for this step couldn't be read because of a writing mistake, such as a missing bracket. It was refused before running, so nothing changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Watch the task for a moment; SMTO usually corrects the code and tries the step again. The message, including the line number, goes back to SMTO's model so it can fix the mistake.
  2. If you supplied the code, look at the line and position named in the message for a missing bracket, quote or colon, or wrong indentation, then send the corrected code. Python stops at the first mistake it finds, and the message points to where it is.
  3. If SMTO keeps producing broken code, ask it in the conversation to rewrite the step more simply or use a different approach. A fresh, simpler version often avoids repeating the same mistake.

What success looks like

  • The Python step runs and shows its result in the task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't send the same code again unchanged; it will be refused the same way.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Parsing the submitted Python source (arguments.code) raised SyntaxError; only the numeric line and offset are reported, and no Python was executed.

What this means

  • Parsing the submitted candidate Python code raised SyntaxError at the source-validation boundary. Only bounded numeric location facts are exported, not source-bearing exception text. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Parsing the submitted candidate Python code raised SyntaxError at the source-validation boundary. Only bounded numeric location facts are exported, not source-bearing exception text.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the candidate source at the retained line and offset; do not attribute an unrelated internal import error to this validation.

How to fix it

  • Use the reported line and offset to fix the syntax in arguments.code, keeping the required main(inputs) or transform(inputs) entry function, then submit a new operation. The parser's own message is withheld so source text cannot leak into diagnostics.
  • Correct the source syntax and advertised entrypoint before execution.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected intended source parses and then passes its separate entrypoint and execution checks.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
